questions.question_text: The total amount of water present in body cavities in a 70 kg adult male is –––––––––– L.
questions.explanation: Transcellular fluid (water in body cavities) accounts for approximately 1 L in a 70 kg adult.

questions.question_text: Among the following, choose the FALSE statement about G protein :

options.C: Dissociates reversibly into two on activation

questions.explanation: G proteins couple to transmembrane receptors but do not themselves act as the primary receptors.

questions.question_text: Which is TRUE about gastrin?

options.C: Acid in stomach increases gastrin secretion

questions.explanation: Gastrin is known to have a trophic effect, stimulating the growth of the gastric mucosa.

questions.question_text: Amount of oxygen carried by one gram of heamoglobin when fully saturated is :
questions.explanation: Each gram of hemoglobin can bind approximately $1.34\text{ ml}$ of oxygen when fully saturated.

questions.question_text: Among the following which is not an action of GH?
questions.explanation: Growth hormone (GH) is diabetogenic and acts to increase gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, and glycogenolysis while generally opposing insulin action.

questions.question_text: First heart sound is heard at :

options.A: At the beginning of IVC phase
options.B: At the end of IVC phase
options.C: At the beginning of IVR phase
options.D: At the end of IVR phase

questions.explanation: The first heart sound coincides with the closure of the atrioventricular valves at the beginning of isovolemic contraction (IVC).

questions.question_text: Which among the following is not a Peptide hormone?
questions.explanation: Oestrogen is a steroid hormone, whereas insulin, calcitonin, and growth hormone are peptide/protein hormones.

questions.question_text: False statement about sertoli cells is :

options.A: Seen in the walls of seminiferous tubules

questions.explanation: Androgens (testosterone) are primarily secreted by Leydig cells, not Sertoli cells.

questions.question_text: Examples of accelerants used in topically applied drugs include :
questions.explanation: Dimethylformamide (DMF), dimethylacetamide (DMA), and dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) are all well-known penetration enhancers.

questions.question_text: For a satisfactory plain tablet the minimum hardness should be :
questions.explanation: A standard acceptable minimum hardness for a plain compressed tablet is generally considered to be around $2\text{ kg}$ (or $2\text{ kp}$).

questions.question_text: The invitro dissolution testing of tablet is to :
questions.explanation: In vitro dissolution helps establish IVIVC, correlates with in vivo bioavailability, and reflects physicochemical properties.

questions.question_text: Promulgens are composed of :

options.A: Mixture of fatty acid and their ethoxylates

questions.explanation: Promulgens are self-emulsifying waxes consisting of mixtures of nonionic emulsifiers such as fatty alcohols and their ethoxylates.

questions.question_text: Phase inversion temperature is also called as :
questions.explanation: Phase inversion temperature (PIT) is also known as the HLB temperature for polyoxyethylated surfactants.

questions.question_text: Weathering of glass containers can be avoided by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Both sulfur treatment and dealkalizing (acid washing) neutralize surface alkali to prevent glass weathering.

questions.question_text: LAL test is how many times more sensitive than rabbit pyrogen test :
questions.explanation: The Limulus Amebocyte Lysate (LAL) test is typically hundreds to thousands of times more sensitive than the traditional rabbit pyrogen test.

questions.question_text: Sunscreen products include which of the following :
questions.explanation: Titanium dioxide, zinc oxide (physical blockers), and avobenzone (chemical blocker) are all standard sunscreen ingredients.

questions.question_text: Equipment used for mixing sticky solids :
questions.explanation: Planetary mixers are well-suited for mixing sticky or viscous pharmaceutical masses and semisolids.

questions.question_text: In fluids at critical velocity the flow changes from Viscous to :
questions.explanation: When fluid velocity exceeds the critical velocity, flow transitions from viscous (laminar) to turbulent.

questions.question_text: Retrovirus mediated gene transfer is
questions.explanation: Retroviral vectors can be utilized for both in vivo and ex vivo gene transfer strategies.

questions.question_text: Type I-hypersensitivity reactions are mediated predominantly by :
questions.explanation: Type I hypersensitivity is an immediate allergic reaction mediated primarily by IgE antibodies.

questions.question_text: Therapeutic index is :

options.A: Maximum non toxic dose/Maximum effective dose
options.D: Maximum effective dose/Maximum non toxic dose

questions.explanation: Therapeutic index is typically expressed as the ratio of toxic dose to effective dose (e.g., $\text{LD}_{50}/\text{ED}_{50}$).

questions.question_text: Myocardial contractility mainly depends on :
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle contraction is triggered by entry of extracellular calcium via L-type channels, which then induces calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum (intracellular calcium).

questions.question_text: Terbutaline is a :
questions.explanation: Terbutaline is a well-known short-acting $\beta_2$ adrenergic agonist used as a bronchodilator.

questions.question_text: An example for ultra short acting barbiturates :
questions.explanation: Thiopentone is an ultra-short-acting barbiturate commonly used for IV induction of anesthesia.

questions.question_text: Abrupt onset of unpaired consciousness associated with staring and cessation of ongoing activities typically lasting 30 seconds :
questions.explanation: Absence seizures (petit mal) present with brief lapses of consciousness and staring spells.

questions.question_text: Reye ‘s syndrome in children seen with administration of :
questions.explanation: Aspirin administration in children with viral infections is strongly linked to the development of Reye's syndrome.

questions.question_text: All are carbonic anhydrase inhibitors except :
questions.explanation: Furosemide is a loop diuretic (inhibitor of $\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+/2\text{Cl}^-$ cotransporter), not a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor.

questions.question_text: A vitamin that work in reducing bad cholesterol :
questions.explanation: Vitamin B3 (niacin) is well known for its lipid-lowering properties, specifically reducing LDL and triglycerides while raising HDL.

questions.question_text: A mitotic spindle poison is :
questions.explanation: Paclitaxel stabilizes microtubules and acts as a mitotic spindle poison.

questions.question_text: A 3rd generation Cepholorosporin used as antimicrobial agent is :
questions.explanation: Cefotaxime is classified as a third-generation cephalosporin.

questions.question_text: The species source for long acting insulins :
questions.explanation: Recombinant human insulin analogues are standard sources for modern short and long-acting insulin preparations.

questions.question_text: An example for anti retroviral agent :
questions.explanation: Zidovudine (AZT) is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor used as an antiretroviral agent.

questions.question_text: Ototoxicity is caused due to :
questions.explanation: Chloroquine (as well as aminoglycosides, loop diuretics, etc.) is known to cause ototoxicity.

questions.question_text: The orphan drug used for orphan disease paracetamol overdose toxicity :
questions.explanation: N-acetylcysteine is the standard specific antidote used to treat paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose.

questions.question_text: The amino acid that does not undergoes transamination :
questions.explanation: Lysine (along with threonine) does not participate in transamination; instead, they are degraded via other pathways.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a Selective $\beta_1$ blocker?
questions.explanation: Metoprolol is a cardioselective $\beta_1$ adrenergic receptor blocker.

questions.question_text: The following is the structure of : (See printed diagram with COOH, NH-CH2, Cl, and NH2SO2 groups)
questions.explanation: The chemical structure shown contains the characteristic anthranilic acid derivative core with a sulfamoyl group ($\text{NH}_2\text{SO}_2$), chloride, and a furfurylamino group, representing furosemide.

questions.question_text: All of the following are substrates for gluconeogenesis except :
questions.explanation: Even-chain fatty acids like palmitic acid yield acetyl-CoA, which cannot be net converted to glucose in humans, making them non-gluconeogenic substrates.

questions.question_text: Globar used as a radiation source in IR spectroscopy is composed of :
questions.explanation: A Globar source consists of a sintered rod of silicon carbide used for infrared radiation emission.

questions.question_text: The most widely used HPLC detector suitable for gradient elution is :
questions.explanation: UV detectors are relatively insensitive to mobile phase composition changes, making them ideal for gradient elution HPLC.

questions.question_text: Mc Ardle’s syndrome is due to deficiency of :
questions.explanation: McArdle's disease (Glycogen storage disease type V) is caused by a deficiency in muscle glycogen phosphorylase.

questions.question_text: The heterocyclic ring present in the structure of Fentanyl is :
questions.explanation: Fentanyl contains a 4-aminopiperidine core heterocyclic ring structure.

questions.question_text: An unsuitable carrier gas in gas chromatography is :
questions.explanation: Oxygen is reactive and can cause column degradation or explosions with hydrogen detectors, making it completely unsuitable as a carrier gas.

questions.question_text: The component of electron transport chain that possess isoprenoid units :
questions.explanation: Coenzyme Q (ubiquinone) possesses a quinone ring attached to a long isoprenoid tail.

questions.question_text: The National Malaria Control Programme (NMCP) became a part of National vector Borne disease control programme in :
questions.explanation: The National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) was restructured around 2002 by integrating various disease control programs.

questions.question_text: The number of pharmacists required for a 100-bed hospital :
questions.explanation: According to standard hospital pharmacy guidelines (like the Health Ministry recommendations in India), a 100-bed hospital typically requires around 8 pharmacists.

questions.question_text: The Secretary of Pharmacy and therapeutics Committee is the :
questions.explanation: The chief pharmacist usually serves as the secretary of the Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee.

questions.question_text: The ISO 9000 standards were first published in :
questions.explanation: The ISO 9000 quality management standards were first officially published by the International Organization for Standardization in 1987.

questions.question_text: The ‘Father of Quality circles’ who introduced the seven tools of quality control :
questions.explanation: Kaoru Ishikawa pioneered quality circles and introduced the seven basic tools of quality control.

questions.question_text: The rVSV-ZEBOV vaccine is approved to prevent :
questions.explanation: rVSV-ZEBOV is a recombinant live-attenuated vaccine used for the prevention of Zaire ebolavirus (Ebola).

questions.question_text: Coconut oil has a very low iodine value and a high saponification value. This is due to the presence of the :

options.C: Triglycerides of smaller quantities of caproic, caprylic, oleic, palmitic and stearic acids

questions.explanation: Coconut oil is rich in medium-chain fatty acids, predominantly lauric acid, giving it a low iodine value and high saponification value.

questions.question_text: Agar is used :

options.A: In the preparation of culture media
options.C: In the treatment of chronic constipation

questions.explanation: Agar finds applications as a solidifying agent in microbiology media, a suspending/emulsifying agent, and a bulk laxative for constipation.

questions.question_text: Fenugreek contains the alkaloid, trigonelline, which is a :
questions.explanation: Trigonelline is an alkaloid derived from N-methylnicotinic acid, classifying it under pyridine type alkaloids.

questions.question_text: Starch granules undergo gelatinization when treated with :

options.B: concentrated solutions of calcium or zinc chlorides

questions.explanation: Starch gelatinization can be induced by strong alkalis and concentrated solutions of certain salts or hydrating agents.

questions.question_text: “Like are cured by likes” is the basic principle involved in :
questions.explanation: The law of similars ('like cures like') is the foundational principle of Homeopathy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the application of plant tissue culture?
questions.explanation: Plant tissue culture is widely used for micropropagation (clonal propagation), secondary metabolite production, and biotransformations.

questions.question_text: All are optically active alkaloids except :
questions.explanation: Papaverine is an achiral benzylisoquinoline alkaloid and is optically inactive.

questions.question_text: Leaf constants are determined by using :
questions.explanation: Stomatal index, vein-islet number, and palisade ratio are all standardized quantitative leaf microscopy constants.

questions.question_text: Shikimic acid pathway is employed by :
questions.explanation: The shikimic acid pathway operates in higher plants, fungi, and bacteria to synthesize aromatic amino acids.

questions.question_text: Ginseng contains :
questions.explanation: Ginseng contains active triterpenoid saponin glycosides known as ginsenosides.

questions.question_text: Both the corm and the seeds of colchicum are used for treating :
questions.explanation: Colchicum corm and seeds contain colchicine, which is primarily used in the treatment of acute gout.

questions.question_text: Urokinase is non antigenic because it is :
questions.explanation: Urokinase is a human endogenous enzyme (thrombolytic) and thus exhibits low antigenicity compared to foreign proteins.

questions.question_text: A marine anticancer agent :
questions.explanation: Bryostatin-1 is a marine-derived macrocyclic lactone with prominent antineoplastic properties.

questions.question_text: Turmeric contains :
questions.explanation: Turmeric volatile oil contains turmerone, atlantone, and zingiberene among its active sesquiterpenes.

questions.question_text: Chlorinated lime is regarded as consisting of :
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder (chlorinated lime) is chemically complex, often formulated as a mixture containing calcium chloro-hypochlorite.

questions.question_text: The reaction by which Indole is converted into 3-dimethylamino-methylindole (Gramine) by :
questions.explanation: The conversion of indole with formaldehyde and dimethylamine to form gramine proceeds via the Mannich reaction.

questions.question_text: DDT is chemically :
questions.explanation: DDT stands for dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane.

questions.question_text: In which heterocyclic ring, the numbering of ring atoms does not start on the hetero atom :
questions.explanation: In acridine, numbering begins at a position adjacent to the central nitrogen heteroatom rather than the nitrogen itself.

questions.question_text: Naphthalene undergoes electrophilic substitution reactions primarily at :
questions.explanation: Electrophilic aromatic substitution in naphthalene preferentially takes place at the alpha-position (C-1).

questions.question_text: Dying oils undergo, which among the following reaction to form a thin water proof film :
questions.explanation: Drying oils harden upon exposure to air through an oxidation-polymerization process of their unsaturated fatty acid chains.

questions.question_text: Meso compounds are achiral due to the presence of :
questions.explanation: Meso compounds contain chiral centers but are overall achiral due to an internal plane or center of symmetry, most commonly a plane of symmetry.

questions.question_text: Which of the following reaction employs amalgamated zinc and concentrated hydrochloric acid as the reducing agent?
questions.explanation: Clemmensen reduction uses zinc amalgam and hydrochloric acid to reduce carbonyl groups to methylene groups.

questions.question_text: Imidazole is isomeric with :
questions.explanation: Imidazole and pyrazole are both five-membered aromatic rings containing two nitrogens, making them isomers with formula $C_3H_4N_2$.

questions.question_text: Phenolphthalein is colourless in :
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless in both acidic and neutral media, turning pink only in alkaline conditions.

questions.question_text: Role of concentrated sulphuric acid in the nitration of benzene :

options.A: To increase the acidity of con. nitric acid
options.B: To avoid the formation of di and trinitrobenzene

questions.explanation: Sulfuric acid acts as a strong acid catalyst that protonates nitric acid to generate the reactive nitronium ion electrophile.

questions.question_text: Assay of calcium gluconate is done by :
questions.explanation: Calcium gluconate is quantitatively assayed using complexometric titration with disodium EDTA.

questions.question_text: Coca derivatives means any mixture of coca containing more than the following amount of cocaine?
questions.explanation: Under the NDPS Act, coca derivatives include preparations containing more than 0.2% of cocaine.

questions.question_text: The import of drugs for personal use contains average dose in mg up to?
questions.explanation: Import of drugs for personal use is permitted up to 100 average doses under specific customs and drug rules.

questions.question_text: All finished alcoholic preparations in a bonded laboratory should be stored in jars or bottles, each containing not less than?
questions.explanation: Medicinal and Toilet Preparations Rules specify a minimum packaging size of 2.25 litres for certain bottled alcoholic preparations in bonded labs.

questions.question_text: Manufacturer of cosmetics to conform to the latest Bureau of Indian Standards requirements is specified in :
questions.explanation: Schedule S of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules specifies standards for cosmetics manufacturing and quality compliance.

questions.question_text: The application to import drugs as part of bonafide laggage is made to the licensing authority in :
questions.explanation: Form 12A is used for applying to import small quantities of drugs for personal use / bonafide baggage.

questions.question_text: The following points should be considered by a pharmacist while dealing with his profession except?
questions.explanation: While being a law-abiding citizen is a general civic duty, specific pharmacy ethics codes emphasize vigilance, limitations of practice, and organizational ties.

questions.question_text: Narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances act was enacted in the year :
questions.explanation: The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act was enacted in India in 1985.

questions.question_text: The number of registered pharmacists nominated by respective state government in a state council is :
questions.explanation: Under the Pharmacy Act, the State Pharmacy Council includes 5 members nominated by the State Government.

questions.question_text: Whoever contravenes any of the provisions of the Drugs and Magic Remedies (objectionable advertisements) Act, 1954 is punishable up to the maximum imprisonment of :
questions.explanation: First-time conviction under the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act carries imprisonment up to 6 months or 1 year depending on the offense clause (typically up to 1 year for first conviction).

questions.question_text: Good manufacturing practices for ayurvedic, siddha and unani medicines is specified in :
questions.explanation: Schedule T outlines the GMP requirements for Ayurvedic, Siddha, and Unani drugs.

questions.question_text: As per the Drugs and Magic Remedies act-1954, which of the disease, disorder or condition cannot be claimed to be cured?
questions.explanation: Goitre, gangrene, and glaucoma are all listed under diseases and conditions that cannot be advertised as curable under the Act.

questions.question_text: Good laboratory practices and requirements of premises and equipments is specified in :
questions.explanation: Schedule L-1 specifies good laboratory practices and requirements for premises and equipment for analytical testing labs.

questions.question_text: The principle fungus for commercial citric acid production by fermentation is :
questions.explanation: Aspergillus niger is the primary fungal strain utilized industrially for citric acid fermentation.

questions.question_text: The certificate of pharmaceutical product is issued in the format recommended by :
questions.explanation: The Certificate of a Pharmaceutical Product (COPP) follows the format established and recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO).

questions.question_text: The rule for permission to import new drug under schedule Y is :
questions.explanation: Rule 122A governs the permission to import new drugs into the country.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is a non-erodible ophthalmic insert?
questions.explanation: Ocusert is a classic example of a membrane-controlled, non-erodible ocular insert system.

questions.question_text: The headquarters of Small Industrial Development Bank of India (SIDBI) is located at :
questions.explanation: The head office of SIDBI is located in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question_text: The parameters for quality Risk management is mentioned in :
questions.explanation: ICH Q9 guideline specifically focuses on Quality Risk Management principles and tools.

questions.question_text: Dose-dependant kinetics is observed in :
questions.explanation: Dose-dependent or non-linear pharmacokinetics (capacity-limited metabolism) is typically described by mixed-order (Michaelis-Menten) kinetics.

questions.question_text: The type of drug administration shown by the following compartment model? $\xrightarrow{k_{10}} 1$
questions.explanation: A single compartment model with elimination rate constant $k_{10}$ directly from the central compartment represents intravenous bolus administration.

questions.question_text: The most frequently occurring value in a data set is called the :
questions.explanation: The mode is defined as the value that appears most frequently in a given data set.

questions.question_text: Coefficient of variation was developed by :
questions.explanation: The coefficient of variation (CV) is a statistical measure of relative dispersion introduced by Karl Pearson.

questions.question_text: Fractional sterilization is also known as :
questions.explanation: Fractional sterilization designed to destroy bacterial spores through intermittent heating is also called tyndallization.

questions.question_text: The biological indicator for radiation sterilization are the spores of :
questions.explanation: Bacillus pumilus spores are standard biological indicators used to validate radiation (gamma) sterilization processes.
